items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: you started playing with Sidney Bechet and Sidney De Paris

ctx.x: Now, the thing that always interested me or intrigued me about your playing career is also that when you left the big band things and settled in New York and played at 52nd Street and stuff... Around that time and a little later, you had the so-called Traditional Revival thing that came in, and you started playing with Sidney Bechet and Sidney De Paris, and eventually even what you call Dixieland. And I guess you didn't play that style when you started. Did you?
I played the style that they played at that time, at the time when I started, and that was kind of like....sort of Dixieland, I would say. Yeah.
